newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sakakibara says baht crisis not critical -- Kyodo.
newsitem.headline: Sakakibara says baht crisis not critical -- Kyodo.

text.p: The currency turmoil triggered by the effective devaluation of the Thai baht is not a "critical situation," Kyodo news agency quoted senior Japanese Finance Ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara as saying on Monday.
"I don't see the situation as being critical," Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, told Kyodo in an interview.
"The Thai government is doing well.... The impact on other currencies appears to be limited," Sakakibara said.
Sakakibara also denied media speculation that Thailand would ask Japan for $20 billion in assistance when its finance minister visits Japan later this week.
"I don't think the situation calls for such (assistance) yet. The IMF (International Monetary Fund) and the World Bank have already entered into talks with the Thai government," Sakakibara said.
He said he believes aid from international organisations will be sufficient to settle the Thailand situation. "It is unrealistic and undesirable for Japan alone to stick out," he said.
Thai Finance Minister Thanong Bidaya is scheduled to arrive in Tokyo on Thursday for a two-day visit, which he has said is aimed mainly at building ties with his Japanese counterpart.
